# A SharedWorker that fails to load never reaches Manager#onWorkerError

> **Premise falsified, 2026-09-23, closed as not planned (author: @neo-opus-ada).** This ticket claimed a SharedWorker that fails to load "reaches nobody". That claim was adopted from `onWorkerError`'s comment ("the ONLY signal…") without being tested. Chrome 152 reports the failure in the **page console** for both kinds of worker: `Failed to fetch a worker script.` for a SharedWorker 404, for a SharedWorker module parse error, and for a dedicated-worker 404. The measurement below (the port binding is dead, and `error` fires on the worker object) still holds, but it fixes nothing observable. Rebinding would only duplicate the browser's own line. The crash slice's *programmatic* start-failure signal moves to #19103. Detail: the `[MERGE_HOLD]` on PR #19104 (comment 5794279240).

## Context

Found on 2026-09-23 while answering a design question on D#18730 ([DC 18564414](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18730#discussioncomment-18564414)). The v13.2 crash slice needs to know when a window group's canvas SharedWorker fails to start. Today no SharedWorker can report that.

## The Problem

`Neo.worker.Manager#createWorker` (`src/worker/Manager.mjs`) binds its error handler like this:

```js
(isShared ? worker.port : worker).onerror = me.onWorkerError.bind(me);
```

For a dedicated `Worker` that is right: `error` fires on the worker. For a `SharedWorker` it is not. A load or parse failure fires `error` on the **`SharedWorker` object**, while `worker.port` is a `MessagePort`, which has no `error` event. Assigning `port.onerror` creates a property that nothing ever calls.

Measured in Chromium 152, with a SharedWorker whose script returns 404:

| handler | times fired |
|---|---|
| `sharedWorker.onerror` | 1 |
| `sharedWorker.port.onerror` | 0 |

`'onerror' in MessagePort.prototype` is `false`. The control, a SharedWorker that loads, exchanged a message and fired no error.

So `onWorkerError` never runs for a SharedWorker, although its own comment (written in #18567) calls it "the ONLY signal for a SharedWorker that fails to load or parse". The binding moved onto the port in 2020 (`9a720bd634`, which switched `onmessage` onto the port to avoid calling `port.start()`), and `onerror` moved with it. #18566's AC-6 later rewrote the handler's body but not where it is bound.

## The Architectural Reality

- `createWorker` creates every worker: App, Data, VDom, Canvas and Task. A worker is shared when `sharedWorkersEnabled && Neo.config.useSharedWorkers`.
- `onmessage` on `worker.port` is correct and must stay: messages do arrive on the port.
- Only the binding changes. What `onWorkerError` logs is not part of this issue.

## The Fix

In `createWorker`, bind `onerror` on the worker object in both modes:

```js
(isShared ? worker.port : worker).onmessage = me.onWorkerMessage.bind(me);
worker.onerror = me.onWorkerError.bind(me);
```

## The Test

Add `test/playwright/unit/worker/ManagerWorkerError.spec.mjs`. `Neo.worker.Manager` reads `window` when its module loads, so its specs run it in a child process with a stubbed DOM. Copy the harness from `test/playwright/unit/worker/ManagerReplySettlement.spec.mjs` (`runReplyProbe`). In the child script:

- stub `globalThis.Worker` and `globalThis.SharedWorker` with a fake class whose instances have `port = {}` and a method that fires a load error the way the browser does: `this.onerror?.({type: 'error'})`;
- before calling `createWorker`, replace `WorkerManager.onWorkerError` with a function that counts its calls;
- set `WorkerManager.sharedWorkersEnabled` and `Neo.config.useSharedWorkers` for the arm;
- call `WorkerManager.createWorker({fileName: 'App.mjs', basePath: '/'})`, fire the error, and print the count.

Two arms:

- **SharedWorker:** the count is `1`. On today's `dev` it is `0`: this exact harness was run before filing, and it printed `{"onWorkerErrorCalls":0,"boundOnWorkerObject":false,"boundOnPort":true}`.
- **Dedicated worker (control):** the count is `1` before and after the fix. It proves the harness can see a call at all.

## How to run it

```bash
npm install
npm run bundle-browser-deps
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/worker/ManagerWorkerError.spec.mjs
```

`bundle-browser-deps` matters: without it the unit tier selects zero tests instead of failing one. **Do not run a bare `npx playwright test`**, because this repository has several Playwright configurations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `createWorker` binds `onerror` on the worker object for both `SharedWorker` and `Worker`; `onmessage` stays on the port for a `SharedWorker`.
- [ ] The new spec's SharedWorker arm is red without the fix and green with it, and the PR says both were checked.
- [ ] The dedicated-worker arm passes before and after the fix.
- [ ] `onWorkerError`'s body is unchanged.

## Out of Scope

- What `onWorkerError` logs, and at which level.
- Errors thrown inside a SharedWorker after it has loaded. Those are mirrored by `worker.Base#forwardErrorToMainThread` (#18566).
- Telling the app worker that a canvas worker failed to start. That belongs to D#18730's slice, which depends on this fix.

## Related

- #18566 and #18567: rewrote `onWorkerError`'s body but not its binding. This is their successor; the closed ticket is not reopened.
- D#18730 ([DC 18564414](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18730#discussioncomment-18564414)): the crash slice's start-failure outcome needs this signal.
- #18985: the Hacktoberfest door this issue is curated for.
